name: Stone-Line Laborer
l1: AP Ability: Stone Line places a Stone marker on an adjacent empty tile. Stone markers are placed objects with 1 HP that block movement.
l2: Causeway Crew: +1 HP. Stone Line may place up to 2 Stone markers on different adjacent empty tiles.
l3: Route To The Surface: +1 MOVE. This character may move through Stone markers. Once per turn after moving through a Stone marker, gain Shield.
role: Common stoneworker, causeway builder, and ley-line laborer. Menka is the named story representative for this common card.

narrative.private_hunger: To build one route that leads his people somewhere other than deeper into hiding.
narrative.relational_wound: His older brother was sealed outside a pressure gate during a flood surge so the rest of the refuge could survive.
narrative.forbidden_attraction: The open surface world, because he has been taught that exposure means death but dreams of sky anyway.
narrative.line_he_will_not_cross: He will not seal a living person behind stone for the sake of tradition.
narrative.line_he_eventually_crosses: He opens a forbidden ley route knowing it may expose the refuge to enemies, because the alternative is letting his people slowly become a tomb.
catch_phrases: Stone does not forget what water tried to take.
Hold the line. The deep is listening.
A wall is only mercy if it has a door.

mechanical_identity: Placed stone objects, ley-line setup, route building, and practical survival.
review_notes: Common class uses an archetypal card name; Menka is the named person in the story.
Profile art should use the horizontal version in the current profile-page format.
Level plan establishes the basic Flood Survivors stone-object vocabulary with disposable 1 HP blockers.

name: Ahesu, the Stone-Current Serpent
l1: Passive: Stone-Current may move through allied Stone markers but must end on an empty tile. If carrying a Hero or Leader, the mounted pair may also use Stone-Current.
l2: Living Causeway: +1 MOVE. If Ahesu starts movement adjacent to a Stone marker, it may move through one occupied allied tile this movement.
l3: Old Route Opens: +1 HP. Once per match, if Ahesu starts adjacent to a Stone marker, move it to an empty tile adjacent to another allied Stone marker within 5 tiles.
role: Named ley-line mount and subterranean transport creature that swims and slides through flooded stone routes.

narrative.public_role: Ley-line mount and subterranean transport creature.
narrative.private_hunger: To return to the unbroken deep routes that existed before Atlantis cut the world into kingdoms.
narrative.relational_wound: It remembers every tunnel that was closed during the Flood, and every voice left on the other side.
narrative.forbidden_attraction: The Great Crystal's shattered pulse, because its fragments still sing through stone in a frequency Ahesu cannot ignore.
narrative.line_it_will_not_cross: It will not carry riders into a route whose stone is already mourning.
narrative.line_it_eventually_crosses: It breaks an ancient sealed passage to answer Menka's call, exposing a refuge that had survived only by being forgotten.
catch_phrases: The road was alive before we named it.
Do not command the deep. Ask where it is willing to open.
Some gates close because they remember mercy.

mechanical_identity: Mount movement through flooded routes, ley-line travel, stone-current paths, and protected transport.
review_notes: Use the grounded card art as preferred because it reads as swimming/sliding through flooded stone routes rather than flying.
Level plan makes Ahesu the stone-route transport piece for Hero/Leader movement.

name: Naia of the Black Sarcophagus
l1: Passive: Tomb Sentinel reduces the first damage Naia takes each turn by 1 while she is adjacent to a placed object.
l2: Sarcophagus Oath: +1 HP. While adjacent to a placed object, Naia's basic attacks mark damaged enemies. The next allied attack against a marked enemy deals +1 damage, then remove Marked.
l3: Open The Black Sarcophagus: +1 ATK. Once per match when Naia would be defeated, if she is adjacent to a placed object, she remains at 1 HP and every adjacent enemy becomes Marked.
role: Named Tomb Sentinel warrior who guards drowned vaults, bodies, bloodlines, and the truths the survivors fear.

narrative.public_role: Tomb Sentinel and warrior guardian of drowned vaults.
narrative.private_hunger: To learn whose body lies inside the Black Sarcophagus and why every record of it was cut from survivor history.
narrative.relational_wound: Her mother was entombed as a holy witness, but Naia suspects she was silenced.
narrative.forbidden_attraction: The voice inside the Black Sarcophagus, because it calls her by a childhood name no living priest should know.
narrative.hidden_relationship: Naia has a secret intimate bond with Sahu-Ren. In public she is his sentinel and jailer; in private she is the only person he lets touch him after a memory rite.
narrative.line_she_will_not_cross: She will not let grave-robbers, priests, or kings use the dead as tools.
narrative.line_she_eventually_crosses: She opens the Black Sarcophagus herself, breaking the oath that made her a sentinel.
catch_phrases: The dead are not silent. You are refusing to listen.
I guard the tombs from thieves and historians alike.
Some coffins are prisons with better prayers.

mechanical_identity: Drowned close combat, tomb defense, guard pressure, death-memory triggers, and sarcophagus/relic protection.
review_notes: Use the corrected profile as preferred because it preserves the card art face, complexion, armor, shield, and weapon more closely.
Black Sarcophagus is a likely Flood Survivor relic.
Level plan makes Naia the tomb-defense warrior who is strongest around placed stone/vault objects.

name: Queen Meret-Anu, Keeper of the Buried Tide
l1: AP Ability: Memory Discipline chooses any allied character. Give that ally 1 Memory marker, max 1 per character. If Meret-Anu does not already have Memory, she also gains 1 Memory marker.
l2: Buried Tide Order: Memory Discipline may target 2 allied characters. If Meret-Anu does not already have Memory, she also gains 1 Memory marker.
l3: Tide-Sealed Archive: +1 HP. Once per match, allies with Memory markers cannot be defeated until the start of your next turn; if one would be defeated, remove its Memory and leave it at 1 HP.
role: Hidden survivor queen who controls bloodlines, archives, ley routes, and the disciplined memory of Atlantis after the Flood.

narrative.public_role: Hidden survivor queen and keeper of undersea and underground bloodlines.
narrative.private_hunger: To preserve Atlantis without allowing Atlantis to become itself again.
narrative.relational_wound: Her mother taught her that mercy is a luxury rulers enjoy only after someone else has made the cruel choice.
narrative.forbidden_attraction: The lost authority of the Crystal Dominion, because part of her still longs for power clean enough to command instead of negotiate.
narrative.line_she_will_not_cross: She will not allow the Great Crystal or its full weapon doctrine to be restored.
narrative.line_she_eventually_crosses: She orders a truthful archive sealed and its witnesses entombed because the revelation might fracture the refuges.
catch_phrases: A drowned crown is still a crown.
Memory is mercy after it has been disciplined.
I did not inherit a kingdom. I inherited the consequences.

mechanical_identity: Relic control, memory discipline, protected archives, sacrifice for preservation, and leader-order effects around stone/ley objects.
review_notes: Use the pristine card art as preferred because the Leader should feel immaculate and power-emitting.
The casket in her hand is the Tide-Sealed Archive, a likely Flood Survivor relic.
Level plan introduces Memory markers as preservation, not prophecy or deck control.

name: Sahu-Ren, Last Memory-Keeper
l1: Passive: Living Archive gains 1 Memory marker, max 3, the first time each turn an ally within 2 tiles takes damage.
l2: Forbidden Testimony: +1 RANGE. Once per turn, remove 1 Memory marker from Sahu-Ren to give an ally within 3 tiles Shield or to mark an enemy within 3 tiles.
l3: Last Memory Released: +1 HP. Once per match, remove up to 3 Memory markers from Sahu-Ren. For each removed marker, heal 1 HP on an ally within 3 tiles or deal 1 damage to a marked enemy within 3 tiles.
role: Living archive and sacred witness who remembers the forbidden truths the Flood Survivors edited, entombed, or disciplined.

narrative.private_hunger: To release the forbidden memory of the Flood without destroying the survivors who depend on the lie.
narrative.relational_wound: He carries memories from people he never met, including children who died believing rescue was coming.
narrative.forbidden_attraction: Forgetting, because peace would mean surrendering the only justice the dead have left.
narrative.hidden_relationship: Sahu-Ren has a hidden intimate relationship with Naia. With her, he remembers his own body, desire, anger, and the possibility that memory is not only punishment.
narrative.line_he_will_not_cross: He will not let memory be edited into obedience.
narrative.line_he_eventually_crosses: He weaponizes a forbidden memory, knowing it will break a refuge's faith in its queen.
catch_phrases: I remember because someone must suffer accurately.
A sealed truth does not become mercy.
When she touches me, the dead go quiet.

mechanical_identity: Memory markers, witness effects, relic truth, reveal without deck manipulation, and emotionally costly return-from-defeat or testimony effects.
review_notes: Relationship with Naia should stay secret, intimate, and dangerous rather than overtly romantic in card art.
Level plan makes Sahu-Ren the memory-engine Hero: he converts witnessed harm into protection or judgment.

name: Iset-Nara, Architect of the Hidden Vault
l1: AP Ability: Hidden Geometry chooses an adjacent Stone marker. Move that Stone marker up to 2 tiles to an empty tile, or give one ally adjacent to it +1 RANGE on its next AP ability this turn.
l2: Vault Surveyor: +1 RANGE. Hidden Geometry may choose a Stone marker within 2 tiles. After moving a Stone marker, one adjacent ally may move 1 tile without spending AP.
l3: The Hidden Vault Opens: +1 HP. Once per match, choose an empty tile adjacent to a Stone marker and place the Hidden Vault there. The Hidden Vault is a placed object with 3 HP. Allies adjacent to it gain Shield at the start of your turn.
role: Sacred architect, ley-line surveyor, and vault engineer who builds hidden archives, false corridors, star shafts, and tomb structures.

narrative.public_role: Sacred architect and ley-line vault engineer.
narrative.private_hunger: To build one hidden archive no queen, priest, or conqueror can fully control.
narrative.relational_wound: Her teacher was entombed inside his own perfect vault so the route system would remain secret.
narrative.forbidden_attraction: Impossible architecture, because a perfectly designed lie can survive longer than truth.
narrative.line_she_will_not_cross: She will not build a vault that destroys the memory it was meant to preserve.
narrative.line_she_eventually_crosses: She designs one that can choose which memories survive.
catch_phrases: Stone is honest. Architecture is not.
A secret needs walls, but truth needs exits.
Measure twice: once for the living, once for the dead.

mechanical_identity: Stone marker manipulation, ley-line measurement, hidden routes, delayed structure effects, and one rare vault set-piece.
review_notes: Distinct from Menka: Menka builds by labor and instinct; Iset-Nara builds by ratio, oath, and hidden design.
Level plan makes Iset-Nara the higher-order structure builder who rearranges Stone markers and opens one important Hidden Vault rather than creating plentiful vault markers.

name: Thalassa-Nekh, Vessel of the Drowned Seraph
l1: AP Ability: Black-Water Communion chooses an ally within 3 tiles. Give that ally 1 Memory marker, max 1 per character, or move 1 Memory marker from that ally to another ally within 2 tiles.
l2: Drowned Judgment: +1 RANGE. When an ally within Thalassa-Nekh's RANGE removes a Memory marker to prevent damage, mark the attacker.
l3: The Drowned Seraph Takes Form: +1 HP. Once per match, Thalassa-Nekh becomes Seraph Form until your next turn. When an ally within range removes a Memory marker to prevent damage, prevent all damage from that attack instead and mark the attacker.
role: Drowned oracle and vessel of a powerful angelic or spiritual entity taken on during a water-burial rite.

narrative.public_role: Drowned oracle and vessel of a spiritual entity.
narrative.private_hunger: To know whether she survived the rite or whether the thing inside her is wearing survival as mercy.
narrative.relational_wound: Her family gave consent to the burial rite, then worshiped what came back.
narrative.forbidden_attraction: Surrendering fully to the Drowned Seraph, because it offers peace, power, and an end to loneliness.
narrative.line_she_will_not_cross: She will not allow another child to be sacrificed to preserve a refuge.
narrative.line_she_eventually_crosses: She lets the Drowned Seraph fully speak through her, and everyone who hears it remembers being judged.
catch_phrases: I did not come back alone.
Your prayers named it holy. That does not make it yours.
The water took a child and returned a witness.

mechanical_identity: Drowned oracle effects, spiritual possession, Memory marker movement, judgment, black-water protection, sacrifice refusal, and transformative Seraph form.
review_notes: The Drowned Seraph should feel angelic/spiritual but older and stranger than a generic feathered angel.
Level plan removes repeated self-damage, lets Thalassa-Nekh use Memory markers, and makes Level 3 a visible once-per-match Seraph transformation.
